sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Flow cytometry on intact cells (PMC7116137): N-terminal FLAG tag confirmed equivalent plasma membrane surface delivery of wild-type and G279S mutant receptors; no impairment of trafficking reported. PMC4513639: construct used for surface expression studies without reported trafficking defect.
sites.rationale: ADORA1 is a GPCR with no signal peptide; residues 1–9 are extracellular and TM1 begins at residue 10. An N-terminal tag therefore prepends before residue 1 (insert_after_residue=0), placing it on the extracellular face. PMC4513639 explicitly states the FLAG epitope was added 'at the N terminus' of the full-length receptor — this is a paper-level citation that names the position. PMC7116137 corroborates with flow cytometry surface detection via the N-terminal FLAG tag on intact cells, confirming extracellular accessibility. The commercial-plasmid disqualification rule does not apply here because PMC4513639 is a primary research paper that independently generated and explicitly positioned the tag. Residue 1 is M (verified from numbered sequence); residue_before is empty (prepend). The tag sits ≥1 residue from TM1 (which starts at residue 10), satisfying the ≥3-residue-from-TM-boundary constraint relative to the tag's C-terminal anchor. PMC4513639 generated N-terminally FLAG-tagged full-length human A1 receptor constructs for surface expression studies in HEK293 cells. PMC7116137 independently used an N-terminal FLAG-tagged full-length A1R (from Sinobiological) and confirmed plasma membrane surface delivery by flow cytometry, detecting the tag on intact cells. [validation: surface_only; position: inferred; source: paper; cited_tag_residue: 0; entailment_verified: True]

sources.claim: In addition, we generated N-terminally modified versions by addition of either a FLAG epitope or a Strep-Tactin II-FLAG tandem affinity purification tag (SF-TAP) at the N terminus ( Gloeckner et al., 2007 ).

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Flow cytometry on intact CAR T cells (PMC12229354): Myc-tagged hA1R confirmed on cell surface by anti-Myc staining; co-expression with Flag-tagged CAR also confirmed. No functional assay of A1R signalling reported for the Myc-tagged construct.
sites.rationale: PMC12229354 reports a Myc tag inserted into the extracellular region of full-length hA1R, validated by surface flow cytometry. The paper uses the phrase 'extracellular region' without naming a specific loop (ECL1, ECL2, ECL3) or residue number. ADORA1 has four extracellular spans: N-terminus (1–9), ECL1 (69–81), ECL2 (147–179), ECL3 (257–267). Because no junction is named, insert_after_residue is left null and region is set to 'extracellular region'. This is a genuine published insertion on the extracellular face of the full-length membrane-anchored receptor and is reported as a region-level site. No residue is invented. Position_evidence is 'inferred' because the junction cannot be pinned from the ledger text. PMC12229354 engineered a short Myc-tag sequence onto the extracellular region of wild-type full-length hA1R expressed in CAR T cells, confirmed by flow cytometry to be on the cell surface. The paper does not specify which extracellular loop or residue carries the tag. [validation: surface_only; position: inferred; source: paper; entailment_verified: True]

sources.claim: Due to the lack of reliable flow cytometry antibodies for the hA 1 R, a short Myc-tag sequence was engineered onto the extracellular region of the wild-type hA 1 R to confirm protein expression on the cell surface (Supplementary Fig. 2 C, and Supplementary Table 1 ).

literature_notes: Ledger lines considered and not proposed as sites: (1) PMC7116137 line 1 — commercial plasmid from Sinobiological with N-terminal FLAG; disqualified on its own as a commercial plasmid with unstated position, but the N-terminal FLAG site is independently grounded by PMC4513639 (a primary paper). (2) PMC7116137 line 3 — eYFP fused to the C-terminus of A1R; the C-terminus (residues 291–326) is intracellular per the topology landmarks, so this does not qualify as an extracellular tag site. (3) PMC4513639 line 6 — YFP-tagged A1R-Y288A; tag position not stated in the ledger clip and Y288 is in TM7 (268–290); likely a C-terminal YFP (intracellular), disqualified. (4) PMC7116137 line 2 — G279S mutagenesis in FLAG/eYFP constructs; G279 is in TM7, this line provides no new tag-position information. The SF-TAP tag mentioned in PMC4513639 is also an N-terminal addition ('at the N terminus') and would map to the same insert_after_residue=0 site as the FLAG tag; it is not listed as a separate site because it is the same junction. No ledger line supports an insertion in ECL1, ECL2, or ECL3 at a named residue.
